narrative: OMX30 enters session with tailwinds from continental Europe's outperformance and a resilient technical setup—bull market regime intact, +5.8% above 200-MA, MACD above signal with strong ADX of 65.2. However, RSI 81.53 and Stochastic K 95.9 signal overbought conditions with mean reversion risk; the index sits at 52-week highs with zero buffer. US tech weakness (NASDAQ -0.74%) and deteriorating correlation from Asia (Hang Seng -0.98%) inject caution, though USD strength and commodity firmness support Sweden's exporter complex. Critical watch: mean reversion off these extremes and US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET could trigger volatility.
morningBrief: OMX30 primed for modest gains on European momentum and solid technicals, but overbought extremes demand discipline. Expect opening support around 3,123–3,130 (yesterday close and 50-MA zone); resistance at 3,160–3,180 (upper Bollinger/psychological). Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken) rally on 5Y real rate re-pricing; industrials/exporters (Volvo B, Atlas Copco, Ericsson B) benefit from USD/SEK strength (+1.29%) offsetting NASDAQ headwinds. Boliden is a key watch—copper +1.24% and gold +0.51% provide direct revenue uplift. Primary risk: overbought RSI and Stochastic leave space for 1–2% pullback if US data disappoints or risk sentiment reverses. Trade the strength into resistance; scale out into dips. Watch 14:30 CET US Jobless Claims.
